fantasy_rationale: LaFleur brings McVay/Shanahan concepts, motion, play action and outside zone. His previous offenses involved RBs heavily in the passing game. Broad positive environment, with the strongest coaching signal at RB.
Rees will call plays within a Stefanski influenced offense. The clearest coaching tendency worth using for fantasy is meaningful TE involvement. Avoid automatically boosting every Falcon.
Doyle is a first-time NFL play caller. Expected play action, motion and multi-TE concepts fit Baltimore's personnel, but uncertainty requires conservative adjustments.
Brady already controlled the offense. His move to head coach does not justify adding another fantasy coaching adjustment.
Idzik is taking over the calls but remains inside the existing Canales offense. Expect continuity rather than a completely new system. Not enough evidence for a preseason boost or downgrade.
Taylor received the OC title, but Johnson remains the offensive architect and play caller.
Same offensive structure and primary caller.
Monken has a strong history of aggressive downfield concepts, adapting to personnel and creating explosive passing opportunities. Do not automatically boost RB receiving volume.
Same primary caller and offensive structure.

Webb is officially taking over play calling while Payton remains the offensive architect and mentor. Potential for a slightly more aggressive passing environment, but Payton's system remains highly influential.

Campbell currently handles the calls, so Petzing should be treated as a scheme/design influence rather than a completely new primary caller. Petzing's historically TE-friendly concepts still give TE a modest positive signal, but the effect is dampened because he is not the primary caller.
Established LaFleur system and play calling.
Caley enters Year 2. No new 2026 coaching adjustment.
Same offensive architect and caller.
Year 2 of Coen's system. Do not apply another coaching bump simply because the offense has continuity.
Bieniemy's return matters operationally, but Reid remains the primary caller.

Strongest coaching upgrade in the league. McDaniel brings motion, spacing, quick-game concepts, outside zone and a strong history of using RBs in both the running and passing games. Coaching should be a legitimate positive tiebreaker on Chargers players.
Coordinator changed, primary offensive architect and play caller did not.
Kubiak has a strong history of emphasizing his best offensive players and maintaining a physical rushing attack. RB and TE are the strongest coaching targets.
Slowik remains within the broader Shanahan/West Coast family, but his history points toward less RB receiving concentration than Miami had under McDaniel. WRs may absorb a larger share.
Same offensive architect and caller.
Year 2 of McDaniels running the offense.
Same primary caller and system.
Nagy will call plays, with John Harbaugh and Greg Roman adding a strong physical run-game influence. RB and TE receive the clearest positive signals, while overall WR volume carries more uncertainty.
Reich's offenses have often used multiple backs and meaningful TE volume. That can reduce concentrated RB workloads and WR target share.

Mannion is a first-time caller but brings Green Bay/McVay influenced concepts and is expected to add rhythm, under-center offense and play action while preserving Philadelphia's established strengths.
McCarthy should shift Pittsburgh toward a more quarterback-friendly and WR-oriented passing attack. Keep the adjustment modest rather than assuming the entire offense dramatically improves.

Fleury is a first-time caller and plans to preserve much of the successful Kubiak/Shanahan structure. His TE background creates a modest TE signal, but there is not enough evidence to upgrade the entire offense.
Maximum offensive continuity.
Robinson brings McVay-style motion, play action and zone concepts. Passing-game structure creates the clearest positive coaching signal.
Daboll's strongest fantasy impact should come through quarterback development and his ability to feature a primary receiver. His history gives less confidence in a concentrated workhorse RB role.
Blough is a first-time caller, so the adjustment stays small. His expected use of motion, under-center concepts and play action provides upside for the quarterback and passing game.
